assets.name: step
assets.prompt:
Edit image 1, the FOUR BODY-ONLY animation parts, using image 2 as the CANONICAL SLENDER BODY PROPORTION reference. This is a precise proportion correction of an existing game sprite sheet. Keep it a 1254x1254 transparent sheet, exactly four body-only poses, same layout, same facing, same action and same two swords per body. NO HEADS; keep empty black collars for separately composited heads.
Problem: the attack bodies look like a bigger, bulkier, longer-limbed man than the idle character in image 2. Correct that while preserving his costume, detailed painting and dynamic poses.
Make the shoulders/chest less broad and thick, the upper arms and thighs slimmer, the gauntlets, hands, knee armor and boots smaller and more delicate to match image 2. The limbs should have the slender youthful adult proportions of the reference, NOT a muscular heroic large-framed fighter. Shorten overextended upper arms/forearms and thighs modestly as needed by repositioning joints naturally; retain the deep stance and weight shift. Do NOT simply shrink the entire sheet or flatten it horizontally. The head attachment, belt center and planted soles should stay in their existing positions; narrow clothing/armor around the underlying skeleton. Maintain the original sword lengths, straight blades, grips, hand/sword positions and blade angles exactly. Do not change the silhouette of the cape except where necessary for the slimmer chest/hips. Keep all four bodies in their existing canvas positions with original transparent gaps. No background, ground, shadows, text, added effects or detached pieces.
Reference image 2 shows the correct body build. Match individual body parts and equipment scale relative to the black collar, not the bounding-box width of the pose. Preserve knees bending and broad foot placement; a broad stance is not a broad skeleton.
